profile.name: Earl Hickson Jr.
profile.eyebrow: EARL HICKSON JR. — LEAD FRONT-END ENGINEER
profile.headline: Designing and building human-centered systems that help people become more capable.
profile.thesis: I design and build technology that helps people become more capable.
profile.belief: Technology should support human capability without unnecessarily replacing human agency.
profile.summary: Front-end engineer with a BFA in graphic design and 6+ years building production interfaces for healthcare, financial services, and digital media. At Asembia, took a fragmented set of HIPAA-regulated patient and prescriber portals from Bootstrap 3 to a reusable Bootstrap 5 component system, and got those standards adopted by the dev team. At BroadcastMed, led design and front-end delivery, mentored junior designers and developers, and built the email system that cut production time 25%. Outside client work, ships tested, CI-deployed products in React, Next.js, and TypeScript. Best where design, accessibility, and engineering overlap, and at getting a team to build the same way. A Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt who has taught students of all ages since 2021; that coaching carries straight into mentoring engineers.
profile.lead: Front-end engineer with a BFA in graphic design and 6+ years building production interfaces for healthcare, financial services, and digital media. I'm at my best where design, accessibility, and engineering overlap, and at getting a team to build the same way.
profile.graduateSummary: Front-end engineer and independent HCI practitioner with a background in graphic design, frontend engineering, and full-stack product development. My work explores how interactive systems can strengthen human capability across relationships, learning, privacy, and complex decision-making without unnecessarily replacing human agency.

selectedProjects.name: Gundam Forge
highlights: Built as a typed monorepo: a Next.js app plus shared packages for game rules and deck validation, a design system, and card-data sync.

Maintains a 623-card catalog pulled from the official card site by a Playwright sync script and validated with Zod, with search, filters, and a validation engine that flags deck errors and warnings as you build.
Playtester with a zone-based battlefield, 100-move undo/redo, keyboard shortcuts, and a computer opponent.
27 Vitest test files cover the rules engine, filters, API contracts, and replay storage; a GitHub Actions workflow gates every deploy on lint and build.

selectedProjects.name: WithYou
highlights: Designed privacy-first: each person owns their profile, invite-code pairing links accounts without merging private data, and sharing is opt-in field by field.

Defined the boundary for a planned AI mediator: it works only from privacy-filtered context and never exposes one partner's private data to the other.

investigations.name: WithYou
investigations.question: How should shared technology support connection without assuming unrestricted access?
investigations.role: Solo product design, UX engineering, and full-stack development
investigations.product: A private relationship application exploring intentional connection, pairing, and field-level information visibility.
evidence: Repository structure and integration behavior demonstrate a working mobile/backend beta.
Simulator and emulator captures show the built interface; prototype references and design sources are labeled separately, and the portfolio prototype uses fictional data.
Evidence supports implemented behavior, not therapeutic benefit or improved relationship outcomes.
limitations: Legacy profile visibility is per account, not per relationship space.
Production builds and a two-person real-device test are still open; the app is not released.
Primary button labels fall below WCAG AA contrast.
No relationship outcome has been validated with a formal study.

investigations.name: Gundam Forge
investigations.question: How can interfaces help people navigate complexity without making the decision for them?
investigations.role: Solo product design and full-stack product development
investigations.product: An independent, unofficial deck-building and playtesting application for the Gundam Card Game.
evidence: Repository and capture evidence support the working deck, validation, and heuristic playtest behaviors.
The portfolio prototype demonstrates warning, explanation, replacement, and recovery using fictional card data.
The implementation does not establish competitive quality, official rules endorsement, or user outcome improvement.
limitations: Official competitive ban/restriction coverage is incomplete.
Public production hosting has not been verified.
The heuristic opponent is a test partner, not generative AI or sophisticated competitive intelligence.
proposedMethods: Comparative completion tasks with and without continuous validation

investigations.name: DojoNet
investigations.question: How can digital systems support progression without reducing learning to completion?
investigations.role: Solo product design and frontend product development
investigations.product: A martial arts training journal and community product centered on practice history, reflection, and qualitative progression.
evidence: Development captures show a working React application and its student-facing journal surfaces.
The prototype demonstrates the difference between qualitative stage history and percentage completion.
The work does not establish that the model improves learning outcomes.
limitations: Instructor workflows require further design and implementation verification.
The current demo persistence model is not a production learning record.
Qualitative stages still require careful language to avoid becoming another hidden ranking system.
